lessonsForFutureWeeks: **Incline DB: 55 across all three sets, by accident, and it held** — died only on the last rep of the last set and finished it as singles. He calls it the new working weight. W25 opens at 55 for all three; the open question is whether the pack-down and the 2s eccentric survived the extra volume, since that's the condition the bump was granted against.

**The dip experiment answered in the opposite direction from the prescription: the ANGLED/V bar is the right station.** The straight narrow bar was 'harder generally and harder on palms'; the angled one 'feels more natural.' The palm pressure was not a hand-position problem to be solved by changing bars — go back to the V bar and stop hunting.

**Two lifts now read as having headroom: push press and the DB lateral raise.** Push press: 'should go up i think getting easy or sitting / static standing' — he's proposing either load or stripping the leg drive. Lateral raise: 'could probably go up' at 15 with the tempo intact, one week after that same tempo made it really hard.

**Cable lat raise directly behind the DB lateral raise is too much stacking** — 'shouldn't have gone right after lat raise omg so hard.' He completed it, but the cable-block rotation restarts next week anyway; don't put the cable lat raise in the lead slot while the DB raise sits immediately upstream.

**Cable column 120 on the straight-arm pulldown is confirmed** — first real datapoint backing that number. The cable lat raise and tri ext ran on the column too, but their numbers weren't recorded; the column number for the cable lat raise is still unverified.
**Farmer carry 'much easier on grip today'** — the grip-limited lift reading easy is the limiter moving. Watch whether it repeats before touching the 50.

exercises.context: 🔆 Warmup spotlight, bodyweight, 6 each side. Depth was the stated project.
exercises.notes: Done. No depth read given — the spotlight prompt went unanswered.

shoulderStatus: No flare reported. Deliberately light overhead day.
lessonsForFutureWeeks: **KB row settles at 50 and stays there.** 'Still easy' at 8 each side, and that's the intended end state — 'tu th is just maintenance, i dont need heavier rows; d3 is row day.' Real row volume lives on pull day. Prescribe 50 and don't hunt for a progression lever on Tuesday/Thursday KB strength.

**The figure-8 → tactical clean got added in unprompted for the second Tuesday running.** W23 programmed it as the warmup spotlight; W24 didn't, and he put it back himself. That's a standing preference, not a one-off — it belongs in the Tuesday warmup by default rather than waiting for a rotation slot.
**Two flows he already knew read as 'really fun' rather than repetitive** — the quality-over-novelty Tuesday worked. Known-flow weeks are a valid alternative to debuting something new.

**Both spotlights (b-stance kickstand, cossack depth) came back with no read.** The reflection prompts didn't land on a day this loose. Either the day was too enjoyable to introspect through or the prompts need to be asked directly after the session.

lessonsForFutureWeeks: **Cable column 270 on the cable crunch was fabricated — the real number is 150.** It was written into the calibration table as 'CONFIRMED W23D3' with no datapoint behind it; the audit shows the column's actual history is 120 → 130 → 150. The table and the drift report are corrected. **The lesson is the one the audit tool exists for: a station with no log datapoint is fabricated until confirmed, and writing 'CONFIRMED' doesn't make it one.**

**The DB row's left-side ceiling moved: 10 at 90 on both sides**, the left as singles. The left grip dying at 8 on the 90 had been the honest number two weeks running. Hold the 70/80/90 pyramid and let the reps keep creeping — this is the floor rising, not a reason to add load.

**Face pull has a new station: single pulley 60, and it was easy.** First datapoint on that stack. The home station is the adjustable pulley + rope at 50. Both go in the descriptor next week; 60 on the single pulley may have room.

**High cable curl 180 on the column read 'pretty easy'** where it was the working ceiling at W18D3. Room above 180 on that station. He calls it the 'double column' — use his name for it in the descriptor.

**Standing logging preference: the behind-back shrug, the warmup and the cool-down are never written down** — 'the shrug is basically warmup; i dont really write it down' / 'i dont write warm up and cool down; too lazy.' Their absence from a report means done-and-unremarkable. Don't ask.
